'''Seymour Jonathan Singer''' (May 23, 1924 – February 2, 2017), more commonly known as Jonathan or “Jon”  Singer, was an American [[cell biology|cell biologist]] and professor of biology at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="Doolittle2017" /> He is best known for co-developing the [[Fluid Mosaic Model]] of the [[cell membrane]], a central concept in modern cell biology.<ref name="Doolittle2017">{{cite journal |last=Doolittle |first=Russell F. |title=S. Jonathan Singer: A man who loved ideas and detested walls |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |year=2017 |volume=114 |issue=14 |pages=3550–3551 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1703437114 |doi-access=free |pmid=28325869 |pmc=5389308}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Singer was born in [[New York City]] and attended [[Columbia University]], where he earned his B.A. in 1943. He received his doctorate from the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]] in 1947. He worked as a postdoctoral fellow with [[Linus Pauling]] at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] during 1947–1948, where he participated in studies demonstrating that hemoglobin in sickle-cell anemia differs from normal hemoglobin, reported in the paper ''"[[Sickle Cell Anemia, a Molecular Disease]]"''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pauling |first1=Linus |last2=Itano |first2=Harvey A. |last3=Singer |first3=S. J. |last4=Wells |first4=Ibert C. |title=Sickle Cell Anemia, a Molecular Disease |journal=Science |year=1949 |volume=110 |issue=2865 |pages=543–548 |doi=10.1126/science.110.2865.543 |pmid=15395398}}</ref> He worked for the U.S. Public Health Service between 1948 and 1950. He joined the Chemistry Department at Yale University as an assistant professor in 1951 and was promoted to associate professor in 1957 and to professor in 1960. There he developed the [[ferritin]]-antibody, which was the first electron-dense reagent used for cell staining in [[electron microscopy]] imaging.  He was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] for Molecular & Cellular Biology in 1959.<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/13614-seymour-jonathan-singer Guggenheim Fellowship] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926105529/http://www.gf.org/fellows/13614-seymour-jonathan-singer |date=2012-09-26 }}</ref>

In 1961 he joined the faculty at [[University of California, San Diego]] as a professor in the Department of Biology (now the Division of Biological Sciences). 

==Research==
At UCSD, Singer's lab conducted studies on the conformation and organization of membrane proteins in the mid-1960s, using techniques such as optical rotatory dispersion and circular dichroism.<ref name="Doolittle2017" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lenard |first1=J. |last2=Singer |first2=S. J. |title=Protein conformation in cell membrane preparations as studied by optical rotatory dispersion and circular dichroism |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |year=1966 |volume=56 |issue=6 |pages=1828–1835 |doi=10.1073/pnas.56.6.1828 |doi-access=free |pmid=16591427 |pmc=224312}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lenard |first1=J. |last2=Singer |first2=S. J. |title=Structure of membranes: reaction of red blood cell membranes with phospholipase C |journal=Science |year=1968 |volume=159 |issue=3816 |pages=738–739 |doi=10.1126/science.159.3816.738-a |pmid=17795071}}</ref> These studies contributed to the development of the [[Fluid Mosaic Model]] of the [[cell membrane]].<ref name="Doolittle2017" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Singer |first1=S. J. |last2=Nicolson |first2=Garth L. |title=The fluid mosaic model of the structure of cell membranes |journal=Science |year=1972 |volume=175 |issue=4023 |pages=720–731 |doi=10.1126/science.175.4023.720 |pmid=4333397 }}</ref> He later studied interactions between the cytoskeleton and the cell membrane, including work on proteins such as vinculin and talin that are involved in linking the cytoskeleton to membranes.<ref name="Doolittle2017" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Geiger |first1=B. |last2=Tokuyasu |first2=K. T. |last3=Dutton |first3=A. H. |last4=Singer |first4=S. J. |title=Vinculin, an intracellular protein localized at specialized sites where microfilament bundles terminate at cell membranes |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |year=1980 |volume=77 |issue=7 |pages=4127–4131 |doi=10.1073/pnas.77.7.4127 |pmid=6776523 |pmc=349702}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rees |first1=D. J. |last2=Ades |first2=S. E. |last3=Singer |first3=S. J. |last4=Hynes |first4=R. O. |title=Sequence and domain structure of talin |journal=Nature |year=1990 |volume=347 |issue=6294 |pages=685–689 |doi=10.1038/347685a0 |pmid=2120593}}</ref>

In 2003, he published the book ''The Splendid Feast of Reason'', which discusses rationalism and the philosophy of science.<ref>{{cite book |last=Singer |first=S. Jonathan |title=The Splendid Feast of Reason |publisher=University of California Press |year=2003 |isbn=978-0520239111}}</ref> 

== Honors and awards ==
Singer was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1969 and to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1971.<ref>{{cite web |title=S. Jonathan Singer |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/s-j-singer-hoduys/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Seymour Jonathan Singer |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/seymour-jonathan-singer}}</ref> He held an American Cancer Society Research Professorship from 1976 to 1991. He received the [[E.B. Wilson Medal]] from the [[American Society for Cell Biology]] and was appointed a University Professor of the University of California, a systemwide distinction, from 1988 until his retirement in 1995.

== Later life and death ==
Singer died in [[La Jolla]] on February 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite news |last=Warth |first=Gary |date=2017-02-08 |title=Jonathan Singer, original UCSD faculty member, dies at 92 |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/education/sd-me-singer-obit-20170208-story.html |newspaper=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]] |access-date=2017-02-11 }}</ref>
